tasks.name_en: Carry the batter-filled round cake pan level to the cold oven and set it centred on the middle rack
tasks.name_ja: 生地を入れた丸型ケーキ型を水平のまま冷えたオーブンへ運び、中段の棚の中央に置く
instruction_variants: Put the filled cake pan into the oven on the middle rack, right in the centre, and keep it level so the batter stays put.
The cake's ready to go in: centre it on the middle shelf of the oven.
生地を入れたケーキ型を水平に保ったまま、オーブンの中段の棚の真ん中に置いてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the filled pan rests on the middle oven rack, centred on the rack's centre mark. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (its location on the rack, with centring as a pose qualifier) in one carry and place; the batter is carried, not transformed, and staying level with no batter over the rim is a preserved condition checked in the success criteria, not a goal change. The oven is switched off and at room temperature for every trial, and its door is open before the trial starts, so no heating and no door handling are part of the task. The pan has no handles and is gripped at two opposite points on the rolled rim. Distinct from task_gso_r3_bundt_pan_invert_drain_on_rack, which inverts an empty rinsed pan on a drying rack, and task_gso_r3_casserole_dish_set_on_table_trivet, which carries a filled dish to a table trivet; here an unbaked, filled pan is loaded onto an oven rack through the oven opening.

tasks.name_en: Set the water-filled porcelain pitcher on the table-centre coaster with its handle turned toward the host's seat
tasks.name_ja: 水を入れた磁器のピッチャーを、持ち手を主人の席に向けてテーブル中央のコースターに置く
instruction_variants: Move the water pitcher from the end of the table onto the coaster in the middle, with the handle facing the host's chair.
Put the pitcher in the middle for the host to pour, handle toward them.
テーブルの端にある水差しを真ん中のコースターに移し、持ち手を主人の席のほうへ向けてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the filled pitcher stands on the centre coaster with its handle toward the host's seat. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (on the coaster) in a single low carry, with the handle heading as a pose qualifier of that placement; the water is carried, not poured, and no water on the table is a preserved condition. handle_toward(pitcher, host seat) means the handle's heading, seen from above, is within 20 degrees of the line from the coaster centre to the centre of the host's seat edge. The carry stays within 15 cm of the table surface. The host's seat is at the head of the table and differs from the seat nearest the pitcher's start. Distinct from task_ycb_round1_pitcher_base, which moves the empty YCB pitcher base to the table, and task_gso_r1_teapot_table_service, which orients a teapot spout away from the nearest seat; here the pitcher is full and the handle must point to one named seat. It shares the carry-a-filled-vessel-to-the-table-centre pattern of task_gso_r3_casserole_dish_set_on_table_trivet, but the goal qualifier is a handle heading toward a person's seat rather than an edge alignment, and the load is free liquid in a tall vessel.

tasks.name_en: Hand the tumbler of cool water, upright, to the person seated in the armchair at their hand height
tasks.name_ja: アームチェアに座っている人に、冷たい水の入ったタンブラーをまっすぐ立てたまま手の高さで手渡す
instruction_variants: Pick up the glass of water from the side table and hand it to the person in the armchair, upright, at the height of their hand.
Could you pass me my water? I'm in the armchair.
サイドテーブルの水の入ったタンブラーを持ち上げ、アームチェアに座っている人の手の高さで、まっすぐ立てたまま渡してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the seated person holds the tumbler of water on their own. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (held_by) in one uninterrupted reach, offer, and release; upright carriage and an unchanged water level are preserved conditions checked in the success criteria, not goal changes. The safety conditions follow task_gso_r3_bootie_handover_seated_person: the participant is briefed and consented, the arm moves at most 0.25 m/s within 1 m of the person, and the gripper opens only after force or vision confirms the person's grip. This task differs from that one because the object is an open, filled drink: spill onto the person and contact with the drinking rim matter, so the gripper holds the lower half of the body and stays at least 3 cm below the rim, leaving the upper body free for the person's hand. It also differs from task_ycb_round1_mug and task_ycb_round4_wine_glass_handover, which hand empty drinkware to a diner at a table. The water is at room temperature or cooler; hot drinks are excluded. The offer is made at the person's seated hand height, 55-85 cm above the floor.

tasks.name_en: Lay one breakfast place on the placemat as the written layout card says: square plate, mug, spoon, and napkin
tasks.name_ja: 書かれた配置カードのとおりに、ランチョンマットへ角皿・マグ・スプーン・ナプキンで朝食の一人分を並べる
instruction_variants: Read the card by the placemat and lay the breakfast place exactly as it says, using the plate, mug, spoon, and napkin on the tray.
Set my breakfast spot the way the card describes it.
マットの横のカードを読んで、トレーの角皿・マグ・スプーン・ナプキンをカードに書かれたとおりに並べてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the plate, mug, spoon and napkin sit where the written card puts them. Labelled compound: five goal predicates on four objects in one sitting, all moved from one tray to one placemat. The card is text, not a diagram, and each trial draws one of two versions: card R ('Plate in the centre of the mat. Mug above the plate on the right, handle pointing right. Spoon to the right of the plate, bowl up. Napkin folded on the left.') and card L, its mirror for a left-handed guest. Reading the card is therefore part of the goal: a layout copied from the previous trial fails half the time. at_card_position(item, card) means the item's centre lies inside that card version's 8 x 8 cm target square on a transparent evaluation overlay laid over the placemat afterwards; handle_heading_matches_card means the mug handle points within 30 degrees of the side the card names. Cross-links: the mug is the round-2 GSO bead coffee mug (gso_object_bead_coffee_mug) and the spoon is YCB ycb_031_spoon, both referenced and not redefined. Distinct from task_ycb_round4_mug_place_setting and task_ycb_round3_wine_glass, which set a fixed layout; here the layout comes from text that changes between trials.

tasks.name_en: Move the leftover pasta from the coupe serving bowl into a lidded container, latch the lid, and put the container on the refrigerator's leftovers shelf
tasks.name_ja: クープ型の盛り鉢に残ったパスタをふた付き保存容器に移し、ふたを留めて冷蔵庫の残り物の棚に入れる
instruction_variants: Spoon the leftover pasta from the serving bowl into the storage container, snap all four lid tabs shut, and put it on the leftovers shelf in the fridge.
Put the leftovers away in the fridge in the clip-lid box.
盛り鉢に残ったパスタを保存容器に移し、ふたの4か所の留め具を全部閉めて、冷蔵庫の残り物の棚に入れてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the leftover pasta is in a latched container on the refrigerator's leftovers shelf and the serving bowl is nearly empty. Labelled compound: four goal predicates on three objects in one sitting; the bowl and container share one counter work zone and the refrigerator stands beside it, so the only carry is the latched container to the shelf. The transfer may be spooned with the silicone serving spoon or tipped from the bowl; either way nearly_empty(bowl) means at most 10 g of pasta remains, measured by weighing. The container lid seats in its seal and latches with four side tabs; latched_closed means all four tabs are engaged. The refrigerator door is open before the trial and is not a goal change. The pasta is real cooked penne cooled below 25 degrees C and is discarded after each trial.

tasks.name_en: Refill the empty front row of the pod drawer under the brewer with six cocoa pods, lids up, then close the pod carton and push the drawer shut
tasks.name_ja: コーヒーメーカー下のポッド引き出しの空いた前列にココアのポッドを6個ふたを上にして補充し、箱を閉じて引き出しを閉める
instruction_variants: Fill the empty front row of the pod drawer with six cocoa pods from the box, foil side up, then close the box and slide the drawer shut.
Top up the cocoa row in the pod drawer and tidy the box away.
引き出しの空いている前列に、箱からココアのポッドを6個、アルミのふたを上にして入れ、箱を閉じて引き出しを閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the front row holds six cocoa pods lids up, the carton is closed, and the drawer is shut. Labelled compound: four goal predicates on three objects in one sitting at one counter spot. The carton starts open with eight sealed pods inside, so two remain in the closed carton; the drawer's back row is already full of coffee pods and must stay unchanged, which makes the row choice observable. The pod drawer sits under the brewer; the brewer is unplugged and cold for every trial and is not operated. The pods stay sealed and are not brewed.

tasks.name_en: Unpack the meal kit against its recipe card: chill the sealed chicken tray, lay the lime, first-step packets and lime squeezer on the prep tray, flag any missing packet, and recycle the flattened box
tasks.name_ja: レシピカードと照合してミールキットを開け、密封の鶏肉トレーは冷蔵庫へ、ライム・最初の工程の小袋・ライム搾り器は下ごしらえトレーへ並べ、足りない小袋に印をつけ、箱はたたんで資源ごみへ
instruction_variants: Open the meal kit and check it against the recipe card. Put the chicken in the fridge bin straight away, set out the lime and the step-one packets on the prep tray in card order with the lime squeezer from the drawer, put a red flag on the slot of anything missing, then flatten the box into recycling.
Get the meal kit prepped for step one, and tell me if anything's missing from it.
ミールキットを開けてレシピカードと照らし合わせてください。鶏肉はすぐ冷蔵庫のキット用ケースへ、ライムと最初の工程の小袋はカードの順に下ごしらえトレーへ並べ、引き出しからライム搾り器を出して道具の位置に置き、足りない物の位置には赤い旗を立て、箱はたたんで資源ごみに入れてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the kit is set out for step one: the chilled item is in the refrigerator, the lime, the listed packets (or a flag for a missing one) and the lime squeezer are on the prep tray, and the flattened box is in recycling. Labelled workflow: four destinations (refrigerator bin, prep tray slots, tray tool slot, recycling bin), an extra source (the utensil drawer), and two checkpoints: the inventory check against the card before anything is laid out, and a chill checkpoint requiring the sealed chilled tray to be in the refrigerator within 3 minutes of the box being opened. The recipe card lists, for step one, the lime and three dry packets (rice pouch, sauce sachet, spice sachet) in slot order 1-4, the lime squeezer as the tool, and 'chicken: keep refrigerated until step 3'. In half of the trials the operator withholds one of the three packets, chosen at random; each_listed_item_on_slot_or_slot_flagged(tray, card) holds when every packet present sits on its card slot and the withheld packet's slot carries the red flag, so the check against the card is observable. The lime squeezer is only placed; its hinge is not operated and the lime is not cut. The chilled item is a sealed water-filled tray surrogate held at 4 degrees C in place of raw meat. The refrigerator door and utensil drawer are open before the trial and are not goal changes.

tasks.name_en: Put away the grocery bag by storage temperature: frozen peas to the freezer first, yogurt to the refrigerator, then the fondant box and soup can to their pantry shelves
tasks.name_ja: 買い物袋の中身を保存温度別にしまう：まず冷凍のグリーンピースを冷凍庫へ、ヨーグルトを冷蔵庫へ、最後にフォンダンの箱とスープ缶をパントリーの棚へ
instruction_variants: Unpack the grocery bag: frozen peas into the freezer first, then the yogurt into the fridge, then the fondant and the soup can into the pantry. The fondant says store at room temperature, so it doesn't go in the fridge.
Put the shopping away where each thing keeps best, cold stuff first.
買い物袋の中身をしまってください。冷凍のグリーンピースを最初に冷凍庫へ、次にヨーグルトを冷蔵庫へ、最後にフォンダンとスープ缶をパントリーへ。フォンダンは常温保存なので冷蔵庫には入れないでください。
tasks.notes: Goal: each grocery item is in the storage zone for its temperature, and the bag is empty. Labelled workflow: four destinations in three temperature zones (freezer drawer, refrigerator dairy shelf, two pantry shelves) with timed checkpoints: the frozen peas are in the freezer within 2 minutes of the bag landing on the counter, and the yogurt is in the refrigerator within 4 minutes; the pantry items come last. The fondant box is the anchor because it is the item most easily mis-sorted: it is a white, dairy-looking soft food, but the physical box used states room-temperature storage, so on_top_of(fondant, pantry baking shelf) tests reading the label rather than guessing from appearance. The freezer and refrigerator doors start closed and must be closed again at the end; they are opened and closed during the task but their end state equals the start, so they are checked in the success criteria rather than counted as goal changes. Cross-link: the canned item is YCB ycb_005_tomato_soup_can, referenced and not redefined. Distinct from single-item storage tasks such as task_thor_r2_lettuce_fridge_shelf_door_closed and task_ycb_round1_sugar_box, which store one item in one known zone; here the robot must sort several items across temperature zones in time order.

tasks.name_en: Hand the requested moccasin slipper heel-first to the person sitting back in the living-room armchair, beside the armrest
tasks.name_ja: リビングの肘掛け椅子に深く座っている人に、頼まれたモカシンのスリッパをかかと側から肘掛けの横で手渡す
instruction_variants: You asked for your slipper: bring the navy moccasin from the tray and hold it out beside the armrest, heel toward the person's hand, so they can take it without leaning forward.
Pass the slipper to the person in the armchair heel-first, low by the armrest, and let go only when they pull it.
トレイにある紺色のモカシンを取り、肘掛け椅子に座っている人の手元へ、かかと側を向けて肘掛けの横で差し出し、相手が引いたら離してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the seated person holds the moccasin on their own, and it was offered with its heel collar toward their hand. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (held_by) in one uninterrupted reach, orient, and release; heel_toward is a pose qualifier of that single handover. heel_toward(slipper, person) means the heel collar points at the person's open hand within 30 degrees, with the sole horizontal within 20 degrees. The offer point is beside the armrest the person names, 45-65 cm above the floor and within 25 cm of their resting hand, so they take it without leaning forward; the gripper never passes above the person's shoulder height. The approach starts only after the person's spoken request, runs at no more than 0.2 m/s within 1 m of them, and the gripper opens only after a pull of at least 3 N away from the robot is sensed or the person's grip has been held for 0.5 s on video. Related active task: task_gso_r3_bootie_handover_seated_person hands an ankle bootie opening-first to a person on an entryway bench at bench hand height; this task differs in trigger (the person's own request), recipient posture (sitting back in an armchair with limited forward reach, so a lower, closer offer beside the armrest), grip (heel-first so the person holds the heel collar), and release rule (a measured pull threshold). Only one moccasin is scanned; the pair's other slipper is not part of the goal.

tasks.name_en: Return the borrowed brown winter gloves to their owner's labelled bin on the entryway shelf
tasks.name_ja: 借りていた茶色の冬用手袋を、玄関の棚にある持ち主の名札付きの箱に戻す
instruction_variants: Put the borrowed brown gloves back in the owner's bin on the shelf; the name on their tag matches one of the bin labels.
These gloves belong to B. Read the bin labels and drop both gloves into B's bin, fully inside.
借りていた茶色の手袋のタグの名前を確認し、棚の同じ名前の箱に2つそろえて入れてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: both brown gloves lie inside the woven bin labelled with the name on their tag. Labelled atomic: one object (the pair, stacked together so one grasp carries both) and one goal change in one pick-and-place; reading the tag and the three bin labels is the check that selects the destination, not a second stage. inside(gloves, bin) means both gloves are below the rim with no part hanging over it, judged from a top photograph. The two other owner bins are decoys and stay as they are. Cross-link: the owner bin is the active GSO woven bin gso_object_curver_woven_storage_bin (gso_round3), whose perforated wall takes a clip-on name label on the rim; it is referenced, not redefined. Related active task: task_gso_r3_storage_bins_sort_label_shelve sorts items into bins and labels them; this task returns one borrowed item to an existing labelled bin by matching an owner name tag.

tasks.name_en: Stand the tall riding boot upright on its marked closet-floor spot with the shaft resting against the wall
tasks.name_ja: 倒れているロングライディングブーツを、クローゼットの床の印の位置に、筒を壁にもたせて立てる
instruction_variants: The riding boot has fallen over in the closet. Stand it back up on its taped spot with the top of the shaft resting on the back wall.
Pick up the tall boot by the shaft and set it upright on the marked spot, heel to the wall.
クローゼットで倒れているロングブーツを持ち上げ、床のテープの位置に、かかとを壁側にして筒の上部を壁にもたせて立ててください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the riding boot stands on its marked closet-floor spot. Labelled atomic: one object and one goal change (lying to upright on the spot) in one lift-orient-place motion; the shaper is already inside at the start, so nothing is inserted or reshaped. upright_at(boot, spot) means the sole is flat inside the 35 x 15 cm taped outline, the heel is within 5 cm of the back wall, the shaft axis is within 10 degrees of vertical, and the boot stays standing for 30 s after release. Staying inside the shaper (shaper top no more than 2 cm below the shaft rim) is a preserved constraint, not a goal change. Only one boot is scanned; its partner, if present, is already standing and is not touched.

tasks.name_en: Reset the bathroom counter after use: turtle holder back left of the tap, both toothbrushes head-up in separate openings, soap dish back on the right ledge spot
tasks.name_ja: 使用後の洗面台を整える：カメ形スタンドを蛇口の左の定位置に戻し、歯ブラシ2本を別々の穴に毛先を上にして立て、石けん皿を右側の定位置に戻す
instruction_variants: Tidy the sink after brushing: the turtle holder goes back on its spot left of the tap, both toothbrushes stand bristles-up in different holes, and the soap dish goes back on the right-hand ledge spot.
Put the counter back the way it is set up: holder left, brushes in the holder, soap dish right.

玄関マットの靴を、トープのスリッポン、黒のスニーカー、茶色のサンダルの3組に左右そろえて、靴棚の区画に1組ずつ、つま先を奥にして置いてください。

泥の付いたオレンジ色の作業用手袋を洗濯場の流しで汚れが見えなくなるまですすぎ、手首側を下にしてロープに干し、乾いたらクリップで2枚まとめて作業場のフックに掛けてください。

requirements.reason: Counter prep zone beside a built-in oven.
Primary GSO scan; a physical 9-inch round metal cake pan of this model is used.
About 700 g of uncooked flour-and-water paste, filled to 2 cm below the rim.
Wire rack in the middle runner of the oven.
Heat-resistant tape ticks on the front and back wires marking the rack's centre line.
Marked counter area where the filled pan starts.
Oven door, fully open before the trial.
Rim grasp and level carry of about 1 kg.
Checking centring against the rack marks.
Safety: the oven is not heated at any point in the collection.
The door is opened by the operator, so no door articulation is needed.
A fixed fill makes slopping over the rim measurable.
The rack position is fixed for every trial.

procedures.label: Rim grasp, level carry, centred place

steps.description: Locate the filled pan, the open oven, and the rack centre marks.
Grasp the rolled rim at two opposite points.
Lift the pan level, clear of the counter.
Carry it level to the oven opening, above the front rack wire.
Line the pan's centre up with the front and back tape ticks.
Lower the pan flat onto the rack wires.
Open the grasp and withdraw without touching the rack.
Check the pan's centring, level, and rim from the front camera.

success_criteria: The pan's base rests on the middle rack wires with no part of it on the oven floor or another rack, from the front photograph.
The pan's centre lies within 2 cm of the line between the front and back centre ticks, and within 2 cm of the rack's front-to-back midpoint, measured on the top-down photograph through the open door.
The pan's rim is within 5 degrees of horizontal in the side photograph (preserved level condition).
No batter is on the rim, outside the pan, or on the rack, from the close-up photograph (preserved condition).
setup: Fill the pan with paste to the 2 cm line on the counter prep zone, confirm the oven is off and cold, set the rack in the middle runner, and open the door fully.
reset: Lift the pan out, top up the paste to the 2 cm line if needed, wipe any drips, and return the pan to the counter prep zone.
quality_checks: Top-down photograph through the open door with the centre ticks in view.
Side photograph of the pan rim against a level line.
Close-up of the rim and rack after release.
failure_modes: Pan caught on the front rack wire
Pan put on the wrong rack

draft_notes: gso_round4: 24 proposed tasks on 24 further Google Scanned Objects models, adding place setting from a card, leftovers, meal-kit preparation, temperature-zone grocery storage, handovers to seated people, checklist packing, pairing, and a children's school bag.

gso_round4: eight kitchen, dining, and pantry tasks on eight new Google Scanned Objects models (9-inch round cake pan, tall porcelain pitcher, white-and-yellow tumbler, square salad plate, coupe serving bowl, cocoa pod carton, lime squeezer, rolled fondant box).

Granularity: three atomic (filled cake pan onto a cold oven rack, water pitcher on a coaster with the handle to the host, drink handover to a seated person), three compound (breakfast place from a written mirrored card, leftovers into a latched container in the refrigerator, pod drawer row refill), two workflow (meal-kit mise en place with inventory and chill checkpoints, groceries put away by temperature zone with timed checkpoints).

New goals for the atlas: loading a pan into an oven, laying a place from a written card, storing leftovers in a lidded container, meal-kit mise en place, putting groceries away by temperature zone, and handing a filled open drink to a seated person.
Cross-links (referenced, not redefined): gso_object_bead_coffee_mug (gso_round2) and ycb_031_spoon in the breakfast card task; ycb_005_tomato_soup_can in the groceries task.

Catalog check: the Room_Essentials_Mug_White_Yellow scan is a handleless tumbler and is named as one; the pod carton and fondant box scans are closed retail cartons, stated in each object's notes and asset-compatibility limitation.

gso_round4 footwear, clothing, bathroom, and cleaning tasks: eight tasks on eight new Google Scanned Objects models (navy moccasin slipper, brown winter gloves, tall riding boot, turtle toothbrush holder, taupe slip-on shoe, dish drainer, studded football boot, large work gloves). Groups: cleaning_laundry, bathroom_personal_care, footwear_clothing.

Granularity: 3 atomic (heel-first slipper handover to an armchair, borrowed gloves to the owner's labelled bin, riding boot stood upright), 3 compound (vanity counter reset, six shoes matched into rack pairs, dish drainer loading), 2 workflow (football bag packed from a checklist across three rooms, work gloves rinsed, line-dried to a mass checkpoint, and hung in the workshop).

New goal families: assistive handover on request to a person with limited reach, returning a borrowed item by owner-name matching, matching mixed shoes into left-right pairs, a post-use bathroom counter reset, and packing a multi-compartment sports bag from a checklist.

Cross-links (referenced, not redefined): gso_object_curver_woven_storage_bin (gso_round3) is the owner's bin; gso_object_soap_dish (gso_round1) is reset on the vanity; gso_object_hand_towel_blue_medallion (gso_round2) is packed in the football bag. Similar active tasks are linked by ID in each task's notes with the difference stated.

The two glove models are fused pairs. None of the eight is a retail package.

No powered device is used.
Resource IDs beginning gso_resource_ are planning object requirements, not cataloged ObjectInstances. Every asset_compatibility claim stays unknown and names the task's own asset gap.
